newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - March 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Liberalisation of wheat, edible oil and sugar imports raise worries of farmers. Authorities will organise one day seminar on March 24 to pave way for commissions which will be in charge of tackling main problems.

- Finance ministry sets a target of 25 percent domestic savings of Gross Domestic Product from current 19 percent to boost investments. French consortium Bossard et Mazars which have been commissioned to make survey on situation, will issue final report soon.

- Cut in interest rates for loans to small and medium-sized firms not enough to trigger economic relaunch. Conditions shaping access to loans should be reviewed as banks earn much money without taking enough risks.
- Newly-inaugurated Al Wahda dam will increase Morocco's water reservoirs' capacity by 40 percent and bring irrigated land to one million hectares (2.5 million acres).
- European Union and Morocco will organise seminar on May 26-27 to promote cooperation projects to upgrade fisheries sector ahead of the free trade zone with EU.
- Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) and Indian firm Chambal Fertilizers and Chemicals to set up joint venture to sell phosphate by-products, due to start operating in April 1999.
- Morocco's stock exchange index rose 30 percent since early January led by the banking sector, ONA and SNI holdings and mutual funds.
